data.content_ref: inline:DEPENDS ON: The isolated problem—determining whether resumption after token-budget exhaustion is safe—depends on SRC_003's two-level invariant as its adjudicating framework, because SRC_003 explicitly identifies that SRC_001 conflates log-level append-only integrity (L1) with stream-level causal continuity (L2). Without this separation, the problem is ill-posed: one cannot distinguish 'was anything corrupted in the log?' (always no, by append-only construction) from 'will the resumed stream diverge from the canonical stream?' (conditionally yes). The problem's resolution inherits this decomposition and depends on the causal fingerprint being deterministically computable from the committed log alone. REFUTED IF: the causal fingerprint depends on non-deterministic system state (thread scheduling, memory layout, cache eviction order) that is not captured by committed events, making L2 unverifiable and reducing the two-level invariant to a vacuous statement where refusal is the only safe option regardless of L1.
